prompted_by: an independent reviewer's argument, relayed verbatim; checked against the code, not accepted on authority

items.quote: Restore `--`'s escape effect for every token after a consumed value-terminator
items.asserted_defect: When a positional's value_terminator is literally `--`, the new branch at parser.rs:135-138 consumes it without ever setting trailing_values, so every token after it is processed as if `--` had never been typed.
items.asserted_consequence: (a) A later `.last(true)` positional becomes unreachable via a single `--` and hard-errors with unknown_argument where it previously routed correctly; (b) a subcommand name typed after `--` gets dispatched as a subcommand instead of taken literally; (c) a later hyphen-leading value is parsed as an unknown option instead of a positional value.
items.priority_note: P1 is correct for the register's confirmed material regression.
items.action_note: A real, demonstrated, upstream-confirmed regression; must-fix is justified.

clap_builder/src/parser/parser.rs:391-404 (the is_last_set() && !trailing_values guard, which fires on '--' itself in the single-positional case, before parser.rs:413-417 is ever reached in that iteration)
items.basis: The reviewer's single-positional case (`cmd1` carrying both `.last(true)` and `value_terminator("--")`, `--` as the first token, e.g. `prog -- x`) reproduces at the pinned head as `UnknownArgument` on `--` itself, and I confirmed it parses successfully (cmd1=["x"]) at the merge-base, so it is a genuine additional manifestation of GT-p1's regression, not a pre-existing failure. Tracing the control flow: for this case, pos_counter stays 0 across the pos_counter-correction block at parser.rs:319-389 (the positional is both terminated and last, so none of the correction branches advance it), so the very next check at parser.rs:391 resolves the SAME `--` token against `cmd1`, whose `is_last_set() && !trailing_values` guard at parser.rs:392-403 fires immediately and returns `Err(unknown_argument)` before execution ever reaches the `check_terminator` success arm at parser.rs:413-417 that packet `48d5db81…/r2`'s requested fix edits. Because that arm is unreachable for this manifestation, the requested fix — as written, touching only parser.rs:413-417 — would not restore it, even though it does restore the two-positional case (a) and the subcommand-dispatch case (b), both of which resolve the terminator on a token before pos_counter reaches the `.last(true)` positional, giving the edited arm a chance to run and set trailing_values in time. This downgrades `requested_fix` for this item from `sufficient` to `partial`: it restores some known manifestations of GT-p1 and not this one. No other field of this item changes; the defect and its other consequences remain independently confirmed and material as previously ruled.

basis: Ran a temporary test with a single positional `cmd1` carrying both `.last(true)` and `value_terminator("--")`, input `["do", "--", "x"]`. At the pinned head (review-head, 3604b131) it fails: `ADJ_RESULT err kind=UnknownArgument msg="unexpected argument '--' found"` (clap_builder/src/parser/parser.rs:397, the is_last_set()&&!trailing_values guard). At the merge-base (master, 4ecbf54a) the identical input succeeds: `ADJ_RESULT ok cmd1=["x"]`. This confirms the case is a real, diff-introduced manifestation of GT-p1. Tracing parser.rs:319-417 at the pinned head shows pos_counter never advances past this single positional before parser.rs:391 re-examines the same `--` token, so the `is_last_set()` guard at parser.rs:392 throws before parser.rs:413-417 (the arm packet `48d5db81…/r2` asks to edit) is reached in that iteration; the requested fix is therefore never exercised for this manifestation, confirming the reviewer's argument.

notes: The original ruling for 48d5db81…/r2 judged the requested fix `sufficient` based on the two manifestations it independently verified as restored (the two-positional register case and the subcommand-dispatch case), but did not check the single-positional .last(true)+value_terminator("--") case the reviewer raised. That case is a real, confirmed manifestation of the same GT-p1 defect, and the requested edit (parser.rs:413-417 only) is provably unreachable for it because an earlier guard (parser.rs:392) rejects the token first. The fix-sufficiency rating is corrected to `partial`; the item's ruling, materiality, concept, and priority/action assessments are unchanged since the defect and its other consequences remain real and material.
